Let $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$g[A] \subseteq B$ and let $f : B \to \mathbb{R}$, so that the composite
$f \circ g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined. Let $c \in A$ be a limit point of
$A$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]) at which $g$ is differentiable
([[def-derivative]]), put $b := g(c)$, and suppose $b$ is a limit point of $B$
at which $f$ is differentiable. Then $f \circ g$ is differentiable at $c$ and

$$(f \circ g)'(c) \;=\; f'\bigl(g(c)\bigr)\,g'(c) .$$

**Both limit-point hypotheses are needed, and neither is automatic.** That $c$
is a limit point of $A$ is what makes $g'(c)$ and $(f \circ g)'(c)$ defined
symbols; that $b = g(c)$ is a limit point of $B$ is what makes $f'(b)$ one.
Nothing forces the second: $g$ may be differentiable at $c$ and send $c$ to an
isolated point of $B$, and there $f'(b)$ is not defined and the formula asserts
nothing.

**No case analysis appears anywhere.** The naive difference-quotient proof
writes $\frac{f(g(x)) - f(g(c))}{g(x) - g(c)} \cdot \frac{g(x) - g(c)}{x - c}$
and then has to say what happens where $g(x) = g(c)$, which may occur at points
arbitrarily close to $c$. Carathéodory's factorisation never divides by the
inner increment, so the difficulty does not arise.

Throughout, $\mathbb{R}$ is the complete ordered field
([[def-complete-ordered-field]]), neighbourhoods are those of
[[def-neighbourhood-r]] and limit points those of [[def-limit-point-r]].

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $c \in A$ be a
**limit point of $A$**. The **difference quotient of $f$ at $c$** is the function

$$q_{f,c} : A \setminus \{c\} \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad q_{f,c}(x) := \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c} .$$

The division is legitimate at every point of the domain, since $x \ne c$ gives
$x - c \ne 0$.

**The point $c$ is a limit point of $A \setminus \{c\}$, not merely of $A$.**
For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ the punctured neighbourhood
$N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c)$ omits $c$, so

$$N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c) \cap A \;=\; N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c) \cap (A \setminus \{c\}) ,$$

and the left-hand side is nonempty because $c$ is a limit point of $A$. So
$q_{f,c}$ is a function on a set having $c$ as a limit point, and
$\lim_{x \to c} q_{f,c}(x)$ is a notion that [[def-function-limit]] defines.

$f$ is **differentiable at $c$** when that limit exists, and then the
**derivative of $f$ at $c$** is

$$f'(c) \;:=\; \lim_{x \to c} q_{f,c}(x) \;=\; \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c} .$$

**Two obligations are carried by that notation, and both are discharged here.**

1. **Uniqueness.** Writing $f'(c)$ treats the right-hand side as a name for a
   single real number. That is legitimate: $c$ is a limit point of the domain
   $A \setminus \{c\}$ of $q_{f,c}$, so at most one real can satisfy the
   $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition, by [[lem-function-limit-unique]] applied to
   $q_{f,c}$. Two reals both meeting the condition are therefore equal, and the
   symbol denotes.
2. **Meaningfulness.** The hypothesis that $c$ is a limit point of $A$ is not
   decoration. At an **isolated** point of $A$ the punctured condition
   $0 < |x - c| < \delta$ is met by no point of the domain at all, so the
   $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ formula is satisfied vacuously by *every* real at
   once; this is why [[def-function-limit]] leaves the limit undefined there,
   and it is why this library defines $f'(c)$ only at a limit point of $A$. At
   an isolated point of its domain a function is neither differentiable nor
   non-differentiable here: the question is not posed.

**The limit sees only $A \setminus \{c\}$, so how the difference quotient is
extended to $c$ is irrelevant.** Let $Q : A \to \mathbb{R}$ agree with
$q_{f,c}$ at every point of $A \setminus \{c\}$, and let $L \in \mathbb{R}$.
Then $\lim_{x \to c} Q(x) = L$ if and only if $\lim_{x \to c} q_{f,c}(x) = L$.
Both conditions read: for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a real
$\delta > 0$ such that every point $x$ of the relevant domain with
$0 < |x - c| < \delta$ satisfies $|{\cdot} - L| < \varepsilon$
([[def-function-limit]]). The clause $0 < |x - c|$ removes $x = c$ from both
quantifiers, so in both cases the points quantified over are exactly the
$x \in A \setminus \{c\}$ with $0 < |x - c| < \delta$, at which $Q$ and
$q_{f,c}$ take the same value. The two conditions are the same condition.

**Differentiability on a set.** For $S \subseteq A$, $f$ is **differentiable on
$S$** when it is differentiable at every $c \in S$; implicit in that phrase is
that every point of $S$ is a limit point of $A$. $f$ is **differentiable** when
it is differentiable on the whole of $A$.

**Restriction of the domain.** Let $B \subseteq A$, let $c \in B$ and suppose
$c$ is a limit point of $B$. If $f$ is differentiable at $c$, then so is the
restriction $f|_B : B \to \mathbb{R}$, and

$$(f|_B)'(c) \;=\; f'(c) .$$

Indeed $B \setminus \{c\} \subseteq A \setminus \{c\}$; the displayed identity
of punctured neighbourhoods above, applied to $B$, shows that $c$ is a limit
point of $B \setminus \{c\}$; the difference quotient $q_{f|_B, c}$ is the
restriction of $q_{f,c}$ to $B \setminus \{c\}$, since $f|_B(c) = f(c)$; and
claim 2 of [[lem-limit-is-local]] carries the limit to that restriction.

**Every point of a nondegenerate interval is a limit point of it.** Let
$J \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex ([[def-interval]]) with at least two
elements and let $p \in J$. Choose $q \in J$ with $q \ne p$, and let a real
$\varepsilon > 0$ be given. If $p < q$, put $y := p + \tfrac{1}{2}\min\{\varepsilon,\ q - p\}$;
then $p < y$, and $y - p \le \tfrac{1}{2}(q-p) < q - p$, so $p < y < q$ and
order-convexity gives $y \in J$, while $0 < |y - p| < \varepsilon$. If $q < p$,
the point $y := p - \tfrac{1}{2}\min\{\varepsilon,\ p - q\}$ serves in the same
way. So $N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(p) \cap J \ne \varnothing$ for every real
$\varepsilon > 0$, that is, $p$ is a limit point of $J$
([[def-limit-point-r]]).

Consequently, for $f$ defined on a nondegenerate interval $I$, the symbol
$f'(c)$ is meaningful at **every** $c \in I$, endpoints included. At an endpoint
the difference quotient is taken over the points of $I$ lying on the one side
that is available, so what other texts call a one-sided derivative is, here,
simply the derivative of $f$ on $I$.

Let $a<b$, let $\varphi$ be $C^1$ and injective on a neighborhood of $[a,b]$, and suppose $\varphi'(x)\ne0$ there. If $f$ is continuous on an interval containing $\varphi([a,b])$, then
$$\int_{\min\{\varphi(a),\varphi(b)\}}^{\max\{\varphi(a),\varphi(b)\}}f(y)\,dy=\int_a^b f(\varphi(x))|\varphi'(x)|\,dx.$$
Thus the absolute derivative is the correct factor for the unoriented image interval.

derivations.claim: [Second derivatives under the substitution] Since $\xi\mapsto\ell\xi$ is $C^1$ with derivative $\ell$ and inverse $x\mapsto x/\ell$, the map $\psi=u\circ(\cdot/\ell)$ is $C^2$ exactly when $u$ is, and by [F1] applied twice, $$\psi'(x)=\frac{u'(x/\ell)}{\ell},\qquad \psi''(x)=\frac{u''(x/\ell)}{\ell^{2}}\qquad(x\in\ell I).$$
[The scale identity] From the definition of $h$ and $W$, $E_\star>0$, $$h^{2}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m\ell^{2}E_\star},\qquad\text{hence}\qquad \frac{1}{h^{2}\ell^{2}}=\frac{2mE_\star}{\hbar^{2}} .$$

[Forward implication of (a)] Suppose $u$ is $C^2$ with $u''=(W-\lambda)u/h^{2}$ on $I$. By step 1.1, $\psi$ is $C^2$ on $\ell I$ and $$\psi''(x)=\frac{u''(x/\ell)}{\ell^{2}} =\frac{1}{\ell^{2}}\cdot\frac{W(x/\ell)-\lambda}{h^{2}}\,u(x/\ell) =\frac{2mE_\star}{\hbar^{2}}\bigl(W(x/\ell)-\lambda\bigr)\psi(x),$$ by step 1.2. Multiplying by $-\hbar^{2}/(2m)$ and bringing $\psi$ terms to the left gives $-(\hbar^{2}/2m)\psi''+E_\star W(x/\ell)\psi=E_\star\lambda\psi$ on $\ell I$.

[Converse implication of (a)] Suppose conversely that $\psi$ is $C^2$ with $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\psi''+E_\star W(x/\ell)\psi=E_\star\lambda\psi$ on $\ell I$. By step 1.1, $u(\xi)=\psi(\ell\xi)$ is $C^2$ on $I$ with $u''(\xi)=\ell^{2}\psi''(\ell\xi)$; substituting the assumed equation at $x=\ell\xi$ gives $$u''(\xi)=\ell^{2}\cdot\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}\bigl(E_\star W(\xi)-E_\star\lambda\bigr)\psi(\ell\xi) =\frac{2m\ell^{2}E_\star}{\hbar^{2}}\bigl(W(\xi)-\lambda\bigr)u(\xi) =\frac{W(\xi)-\lambda}{h^{2}}u(\xi),$$ the last equality by step 1.2.

[The exponent identity (b)] On $[a,b]$ the function $x\mapsto\ell x$ is $C^1$ and strictly increasing with derivative $\ell>0$, and the integrand $f(x):=\sqrt{2m(E_\star W(x/\ell)-E_\star\lambda)}$ is continuous on $[\ell a,\ell b]$ because $W$ is continuous and $W-\lambda>0$. By [F2] applied to $\varphi(\xi)=\ell\xi$, $$\int_{\ell a}^{\ell b}\sqrt{2m(E_\star W(x/\ell)-E_\star\lambda)}\,dx =\int_a^b\sqrt{2mE_\star\bigl(W(\xi)-\lambda\bigr)}\,\ell\,d\xi =\sqrt{2mE_\star}\,\ell\int_a^b\sqrt{W(\xi)-\lambda}\,d\xi .$$ Dividing by $\hbar$ and using $\frac{\sqrt{2mE_\star}\,\ell}{\hbar}=\frac1h$ from the definition of $h$ gives (b).

boundaries.reason: The lemma concerns a nonempty open interval I and a physical interval [a,b] with a<b; no empty-set case is asserted.
The scales are strictly positive and the lemma contains no special value at zero of any parameter.
No unit parameter is distinguished; the identities hold for every admissible scale and every lambda.
The only degenerate configurations excluded are W-lambda=0 on [a,b] in clause (b), which is stated as a hypothesis rather than claimed; no degenerate case is left to check.

citations.quote: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on the nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$. Then there is a unique regular projection valued measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that $$ D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)). $$ Conversely, if $E$ is a regular projection valued measure on $\mathbb R$, then the operator $\int\lambda\,dE$ with that domain is self-adjoint and its spectral projection valued measure is $E$ again.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space ([[def-measurable-space]], [[def-sigma-algebra]]) and let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). A **projection valued measure** (PVM) on $(X,\Sigma)$ is a map $$E:\Sigma\longrightarrow\mathcal B(H),\qquad B\longmapsto E(B),$$ such that: 1. $E(B)$ is an **orthogonal projection** for every $B\in\Sigma$, that is, a bounded operator with $E(B)^2=E(B)=E(B)^*$; there is no finite-dimensional restriction; 2. $E(\varnothing)=0$ and $E(X)=I$; 3. $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$ for all $B,C\in\Sigma$; 4. for every pairwise disjoint sequence $(B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ in $\Sigma$ with union $B$ and every $x\in H$, the series $\sum_nE(B_n)x$ converges in norm to $E(B)x$, that is $$E(B)x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}E(B_n)x .$$ Clause 4 is **strong countable additivity**. A PVM is called **regular** when $X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]), the $\sigma$-algebra is the Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and every one of the finite positive measures $$E_x(B):=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle,\qquad x\in H,\ B\in\Sigma,$$ is a regular Borel measure ([[def-regular-borel-measure-on-an-lch-space]]). Inner products are linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]); this fixed convention is the one used for every pairing $E_{x,y}(B)=\langle E(B)x,y\rangle$ on this page. **Well-definedness: the projection clause.** The conditions $P^2=P=P^*$ are simultaneously meaningful and describe exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections, with no hidden finite-dimensional hypothesis. Indeed, for a bounded $P$ with $P^2=P=P^*$ the range $\operatorname{ran}P$ is a linear subspace, and for $y=Pw$ one has $\langle x-Px,y\rangle=\langle P(x-Px),w\rangle=\langle Px-P^2x,w\rangle=0$, so $x-Px\perp\operatorname{ran}P$; conversely $\langle Pz,Pz\rangle=\langle z,P^*Pz\rangle=\langle z,Pz\rangle=0$ for $z\perp\operatorname{ran}P$, so $z\in\ker P$, while $\langle z,Px\rangle=\langle Pz,x\rangle=0$ for $z\in\ker P$ gives $\ker P=(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$ ([[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Hence $\operatorname{ran}P=(\ker P)^\perp$ is closed, and the two defining properties $Px\in\operatorname{ran}P$, $x-Px\in(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$ of [[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]] show that $P=P_{\operatorname{ran}P}$ is the Hilbert orthogonal projection onto a closed subspace, and conversely every such $P_M$ is idempotent and self-adjoint by [[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]] and [[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]. Finally $P$ is contractive: from $\langle Px,x\rangle=\langle Px,Px\rangle=\|Px\|^2$ and Cauchy–Schwarz, $\|Px\|^2\le\|Px\|\,\|x\|$, so $\|Px\|\le\|x\|$ for all $x$, and $\langle Px,x\rangle=\|Px\|^2\ge0$ is a nonnegative real number. **Well-definedness: the regularity clause.** For an orthogonal projection value the pairing $E_x(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle$ is a nonnegative real number and $E_x(X)=\langle x,x\rangle=\|x\|^2<+\infty$, so every $E_x$ is a finite nonnegative set function and the regularity requirement is a meaningful condition on it; that each $E_x$ is genuinely a countably additive measure of total mass $\|x\|^2$, and that the polarized pairings $E_{x,y}$ are finite complex measures, is proved as [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]] before either is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on a complex Hilbert space $H$ with spectral projection valued measure $E$ on $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). The **discrete spectrum** $\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)$ is the set of eigenvalues of $A$ that are isolated points of $\sigma(A)$ and whose eigenspace is finite dimensional; the **essential spectrum** is $$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A):=\sigma(A)\setminus\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A),$$ with $\sigma(A)$ as in [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]]. For $H=\{0\}$ use its unique PVM directly: the spectrum and both parts are empty and every projection has rank zero. Below suppose $H\ne\{0\}$, as required by the cited spectral theorem. **Spectral-projection description, with proofs.** Fix $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and write $P_\varepsilon:=E((\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon))$ for $\varepsilon>0$. Here rank means the algebraic dimension of the range when finite; rank $=\infty$ means the range is not finite dimensional. The calculus [[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]] gives the support facts: $E(\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(A))=0$, and every open interval about a spectral point has nonzero projection. Projections on disjoint sets have orthogonal ranges, and $E(B)E(C)=E(B\cap C)$ [[def-projection-valued-measure]]. 1. *$E(\{\lambda\})$ is the projection onto $\ker(A-\lambda)$.* If $x=E(\{\lambda\})x$, its scalar measure $E_x$ is supported on $\{\lambda\}$ by the projection identity. Thus $\int\mu^2dE_x=\lambda^2\|x\|^2<\infty$, so $x\in D(A)$, and $$\|(A-\lambda)x\|^2=\int|\mu-\lambda|^2dE_x=0.$$ The domain and norm identities are supplied by the unbounded calculus and [[lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed]]. Hence $Ax=\lambda x$. Conversely, for an eigenvector (or the zero vector) the same norm identity gives zero integral. On $\{|\mu-\lambda|\ge1/n\}$ this bounds the measure by $n^2$ times that zero integral; taking the countable union shows $E_x(\mathbb R\setminus\{\lambda\})=0$. Since $\|(I-E(\{\lambda\}))x\|^2$ equals this scalar measure, $E(\{\lambda\})x=x$. 2. *A finite-rank interval contains only finitely many spectral points.* If $P_\varepsilon$ has rank $r<\infty$ and its interval contained $r+1$ distinct spectral points, choose disjoint small open intervals about those finitely many points, all contained in the given interval. Each has a nonzero projection by support. Choose one unit vector in each range. They are orthonormal vectors in $\operatorname{ran}P_\varepsilon$, hence linearly independent (take inner products with each vector), contradicting its dimension $r$. Thus there are at most $r$ spectral points there. In particular any $\lambda\in\sigma(A)$ with such a finite-rank $P_\varepsilon$ is isolated: take a smaller interval around $\lambda$ excluding the other finitely many points. For that interval the projection is $E(\{\lambda\})$ by support, is nonzero by support, and has finite rank since its range lies in $\operatorname{ran}P_\varepsilon$. By item 1, $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of finite multiplicity. 3. *The two rank characterizations.* If $\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)$, an isolating interval has projection $E(\{\lambda\})$, of finite rank by item 1. Conversely, if $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue and some $P_\varepsilon$ has finite rank, item 2 proves it discrete. Hence $$\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\lambda\text{ is an eigenvalue and some }P_\varepsilon\text{ has finite rank}.$$ If $\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$, item 2 excludes every finite-rank interval. Conversely, if every $P_\varepsilon$ has infinite rank, each is nonzero, so support puts $\lambda$ in $\sigma(A)$, and the just-proved discrete characterization excludes it from $\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)$. Therefore $$\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{rank}P_\varepsilon=\infty\text{ for every }\varepsilon>0.$$ 4. *$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$ is closed.* If $\lambda_n\in \sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$ and $\lambda_n\to\lambda$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ some $n$ has $(\lambda_n-\varepsilon/2, \lambda_n+ \varepsilon/2)\subseteq(\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon)$, so $\operatorname{rank}P_\varepsilon\ge\operatorname{rank}P_{\varepsilon/2}^{(n)} =\infty$ and $\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$ by item 3. The closure conclusion is in $\mathbb R$, and also in $\mathbb C$ since $\mathbb R$ is closed there. A spectral accumulation point has infinitely many spectral points in every surrounding interval, so item 2 forces infinite rank. An isolated eigenvalue of infinite multiplicity has its infinite-dimensional eigenspace inside every interval range by item 1. Consequently an accumulation point of $\sigma(A)$ and an isolated eigenvalue of infinite multiplicity both lie in $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$, and $\sigma(A)$ is the disjoint union of $\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)$ and $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A$ be self-adjoint on a complex Hilbert space H, with $A\ge cI$ meaning $\langle Ax,x\rangle\ge c\|x\|^2$ for every $x\in D(A)$, for some real $c$. Put $$Q(A):=D\bigl((A-cI)^{1/2}\bigr),\qquad q_A[x]:=c\|x\|^2+\bigl\|(A-cI)^{1/2}x\bigr\|^2\quad(x\in Q(A)).$$ Then $Q(A)$ and $q_A$ do not depend on the choice of the constant $c\le\inf\sigma(A)$ (the form $q_A[x]=\int\lambda\,dE_x$ is itself unchanged, while the summand $\|(A-cI)^{1/2}x\|^2$ changes by the constant $(c-c')\|x\|^2$ when $c$ is replaced by $c'\le c$), $q_A[x]=\int\lambda\,dE_x(\lambda)=\langle Ax,x\rangle$ for $x\in D(A)$, the domain $D(A)$ is dense in $Q(A)$ for the norm $\|x\|_Q=(\|x\|^2+\|(A-cI)^{1/2}x\|^2)^{1/2}$, and $q_A$ is a closed quadratic form with $q_A[x]\ge c\|x\|^2$. Here the square root is the Borel calculus of $\sqrt{\max(\lambda-c,0)}$; the proof shows that E is carried on $[c,\infty)$. A closed semibounded quadratic form means the diagonal of a Hermitian sesquilinear form on a dense linear domain, complete in the displayed shifted form norm. If H={0}, use the unique PVM and operator and the convention inf(empty spectrum)=+infinity.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Assume the Axiom of Choice. citations.quote: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Work on a complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first variable. Let $A$ be self-adjoint and let $B$ be symmetric with $D(A)\subseteq D(B)$ and $A$-bound less than one ([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]]). Then $A+B$ with domain $D(A)$ is self-adjoint. If $A$ is merely essentially self-adjoint and $B$ is symmetric with $D(A)\subseteq D(B)$ and $A$-bound less than one, then $A+B$ on $D(A)$ is essentially self-adjoint and its closure is the self-adjoint operator obtained by applying the first part to $\overline A$ and the graph-norm extension of $B|_{D(A)}$ to $D(\overline A)$. If $A\ge\gamma$ and $(a,b)$ is an admissible pair for $B$ with $a<1$, then $A+B\ge\gamma-\max\{a|\gamma|+b,\ b/(1-a)\}$.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be an arbitrary complex Hilbert space, let $H_0$ be self-adjoint on its exact dense domain, and use the resolvent convention $R_0(z)=(z-H_0)^{-1}$. Let $E\in\mathbb R$ be an isolated eigenvalue with $\operatorname{dist}(E,\sigma(H_0)\setminus\{E\})\ge g>0$, and suppose its orthogonal spectral projection $P_0=E_{H_0}(\{E\})$ has rank one. Let $V\in\mathcal B(H)$ be self-adjoint with $v=\|V\|>0$, put $H_\lambda=H_0+\lambda V$ on $D(H_0)$, and let $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ satisfy $q=2|\lambda|v/g<1$. Write $\Gamma$ for the counterclockwise circle $|z-E|=g/2$. Then: (a) $H_\lambda$ is closed and densely defined. For every $z\in\Gamma$, $z-H_\lambda$ is a bijection from $D(H_0)$ onto $H$, with $$R_\lambda(z)=(z-H_\lambda)^{-1}=R_0(z)\sum_{k\ge0}(\lambda VR_0(z))^k,\qquad \|R_\lambda(z)\|\le\frac{2/g}{1-q},\qquad \|R_\lambda(z)-R_0(z)\|\le\frac{2}{g}\frac{q}{1-q}.$$ The series converges in operator norm uniformly on $\Gamma$ and locally uniformly in the complex disk $|\lambda|<g/(2v)$. (b) The operator $$P_\lambda=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint_\Gamma R_\lambda(z)dz$$ is an operator-norm holomorphic, rank-one Riesz projection throughout that disk. Its range lies in $D(H_0)$ and is invariant under $H_\lambda$, and it commutes with $H_\lambda$ on $D(H_0)$. There is exactly one spectral value $E_\lambda$ inside $\Gamma$; it is an eigenvalue of algebraic multiplicity one, with $\operatorname{ran}P_\lambda=\ker(H_\lambda-E_\lambda)$. The function $\lambda\mapsto E_\lambda$ is holomorphic. (c) $\|P_\lambda-P_0\|\le q/(1-q)$. Rank one holds for every $q<1$, including when this bound is at least one. Whenever two projections $P_\lambda,P_\mu$ have distance less than one, the restrictions $P_\mu|_{\operatorname{ran}P_\lambda}$ and $P_\lambda|_{\operatorname{ran}P_\mu}$ are injective; local comparisons along the path $t\lambda$, $0\le t\le1$, preserve the rank throughout the full disk. (d) For real $\lambda$, $H_\lambda$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_0)$, $E_\lambda$ is real, and $P_\lambda=E_{H_\lambda}(\{E_\lambda\})$ is its orthogonal spectral projection. For complex $\lambda$, $P_\lambda$ is the Riesz projection; self-adjointness or orthogonality is not asserted. No separability or Axiom of Choice assumption on $H$ is added. Degenerate clusters are outside this rank-one statement.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and adopt the hypotheses of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-contour-perturbation-projection]]: $H_0$ self-adjoint with isolated simple eigenvalue $E$, gap $g>0$, normalized eigenvector $\psi_0$ with $P_0\psi_0=\psi_0$, $V=V^*\in\mathcal B(H)$ with $v=\|V\|$, and $q=2|\lambda|v/g<1/2$. Write $Q=I-P_0$, $H_Q=H_0|_{D(H_0)\cap QH}$ on the reducing space $QH$, and define the reduced inverse $$S=\iota_Q(H_Q-E)^{-1}Q:H\longrightarrow D(H_0)\cap QH,$$ where $\iota_Q:QH\hookrightarrow H$ is the inclusion (and the zero complementary space gives the zero map). Then $S$ is bounded with $\|S\|\le1/g$; no inverse of $H_0-E$ on all of $H$ is asserted. Let $P_\lambda$, $E_\lambda$ be the perturbed projection and its unique eigenvalue inside the contour, as in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-contour-perturbation-projection]]. Define the gauge-normalized eigenvector $$\psi(\lambda):=\frac{P_\lambda\psi_0}{\langle P_\lambda\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle}.$$ Then $\psi(\lambda)$ is analytic in $\lambda$ with $\|\psi(\lambda)\|\le3$ for $q<1/2$, $\langle\psi(\lambda),\psi_0\rangle=1$, and $(H_0+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda)=E_\lambda\psi(\lambda)$. Moreover the first and second coefficients are $$E'(0)=\langle V\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle,\qquad \psi'(0)=-SV\psi_0,\qquad E''(0)=-2\langle VSV\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle,$$ where all pairings are finite and the second derivative involves the whole complementary spectral subspace, not only bound states. Equivalently $E_\lambda=E+\lambda\langle V\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle-\lambda^2\langle VSV\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle+O(\lambda^3)$ for $|\lambda|$ in the disk of the remainder estimate; the $O(\lambda^3)$ is made explicit in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-analytic-perturbation-remainder]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the hypotheses of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-simple-level-reduced-resolvent-coefficients]] on an arbitrary complex Hilbert space $H$, with inner product linear in the first variable: $H_0$ is self-adjoint on its exact dense domain, $E$ is an isolated simple eigenvalue with gap at least $g>0$, $\psi_0$ is a normalized eigenvector, and $V=V^*$ is bounded with $v=\|V\|$. Let $P_\lambda,E_\lambda$ be the contour projection and eigenvalue, $Q=I-P_0$, $S=\iota_Q(H_0|_{D(H_0)\cap QH}-E)^{-1}Q$ the actual reduced inverse, and $\psi(\lambda)$ the gauge-fixed eigenvector with $\langle\psi(\lambda),\psi_0\rangle=1$. For $v>0$ put $R=g/(8v)$. On the full complex disk $|\lambda|<R$: (a) $q=2|\lambda|v/g\le1/4$, $\|P_\lambda-P_0\|\le1/3$, $\|\psi(\lambda)\|\le2$, and the holomorphic scalar energy identity is $$E_\lambda=\langle(H_0+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda),\psi_0\rangle=E+\lambda\langle V\psi(\lambda),\psi_0\rangle.$$ (b) The exact coefficients are $$E'(0)=\langle V\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle,\qquad \psi'(0)=-SV\psi_0,\qquad E''(0)=-2\langle VSV\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle,$$ with bounds $|E'(0)|\le v$, $\|\psi'(0)\|\le v/g$ and $|E''(0)|\le2v^2/g$. The whole complementary spectral subspace, including its continuum, contributes through $S$. The cubic remainder satisfies $$\left|E_\lambda-E-\lambda E'(0)-\frac{\lambda^2}{2}E''(0)\right|\le\frac{Rv\,(|\lambda|/R)^3}{1-|\lambda|/R}.$$ At $|\lambda|=R/2$ the displayed bound is $Rv/4=g/32$. For $|\lambda|\le R/2$ it is at most $128v^3|\lambda|^3/g^2$. (c) If $v=0$, then $V=0$ and $P_\lambda=P_0$, $E_\lambda=E$, $\psi(\lambda)=\psi_0$ for every complex $\lambda$; no radius involving division by $v$ is used in this branch. These conclusions are conditional on the strict positive gap and bounded perturbation, and do not assert an unbounded or degenerate perturbation theorem.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt P1, P2 and P4 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, with the state, sharp-observable and evolution readings of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical suppliers. **(b) The perturbed family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair, fix a self-adjoint operator $H_{0}:D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H\to\mathfrak H$ on the declared state space, **declare** $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ to be the unperturbed sharp energy observable, fix a bounded self-adjoint operator $V\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) with $$v:=\|V\|<\infty$$ ([[def-operator-norm]]) and fix a real **coupling** $\lambda$ (dimensionless: $\lambda V$ is read in joules). Declare the **perturbed family** $$H(\lambda):=H_{0}+\lambda V,\qquad D(H(\lambda)):=D(H_{0}),$$ to be the model's sharp energy observable at coupling $\lambda$. Since $V$ is $H_{0}$-bounded with $H_{0}$-bound $0\le a<1$ (the bound inequality holds with $a=0$ and $b=v$), the Kato-Rellich theorem applies and $H(\lambda)$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$ for every real $\lambda$ ([[thm-kato-rellich]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). This self-adjointness is a supplied theorem about the declared operators; the reading of the family as the system's energy is the model assumption. **(c) The gapped label.** Fix an isolated eigenvalue $E\in\mathbb R$ of $H_{0}$ of finite multiplicity $r\ge1$ with gap $$\operatorname{dist}\bigl(E,\sigma(H_{0})\setminus\{E\}\bigr)\ge g>0,$$ and put $P_{0}:=E_{H_{0}}(\{E\})$ and $Q_{0}:=I-P_{0}$ ([[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]]). The definitions used by the pair are those of the cited suppliers: (i) for real $\lambda$ with $2|\lambda|v/g<1$, the **followed spectral cluster** is the spectrum of $H(\lambda)$ inside $|z-E|<g/2$, and $$P_\lambda:=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{|z-E|=g/2}(z-H(\lambda))^{-1}\,dz$$ (counterclockwise) is its rank-$r$ orthogonal spectral projection, by [[lem-nrqm-approximations-finite-rank-gapped-cluster-projection]]. The cluster is a nonempty finite set and is exactly the spectrum of the restriction to $P_\lambda\mathfrak H$. In the simple case $r=1$ only, write $E_\lambda$ for its unique spectral value; this scalar is the followed perturbed label of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-contour-perturbation-projection]] and is analytic on the valid coupling disk. For $r>1$ no unique scalar label, branch ordering or individual scalar holomorphy is presumed. At $\lambda=0$ the cluster is $\{E\}$ and its projection is $P_0$. If $v=0$, these data are constant for all real couplings, with no radius involving division by $v$. (ii) the **first-order operator** is the Hermitian operator $$V_{E}:=\bigl(P_{0}VP_{0}\bigr)\big|_{P_{0}\mathfrak H}$$ on the finite-dimensional eigenspace $P_{0}\mathfrak H$, whose spectrum $\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})\subseteq[-v,v]$ is the model's first-order shift data (joules per unit coupling); (iii) the **complementary reduced inverse** $$S:=\iota_{Q_{0}}\bigl(H_{0}|_{D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H}-E\bigr)^{-1}Q_{0}$$ is a bounded operator with the displayed exact complementary-domain inverse. For $r=1$ it is supplied by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-simple-level-reduced-resolvent-coefficients]]; for general finite $r$ it is $\iota_{Q_0}B_0(E)Q_0$, where $B_0(E)$ is the inverse in clause (a) of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-degenerate-feshbach-error]] at zero coupling and $z=E$. Its role is to record that the **whole** complementary spectral subspace, continuum included, contributes to the second-order data. **(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) cover bounded perturbations of a self-adjoint operator and a fixed isolated finite-multiplicity label only. The definition asserts no time-dependent perturbation, no adiabatic ramping of $\lambda$, no statement that a preparation occupies the branch of $E_{\lambda}$ or of any eigenvalue of $V_{E}$, no branch-population or relaxation statement, no measurement and no identification of the model with a laboratory system; the labels $E_{\lambda}$ are spectral data of the declared family.

Let $V\in C_c^5(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$ be fixed and let $E>0$ be such that
$V-E$ has exactly two simple zeros $a<b$, is positive on $(a,b)$ and negative
outside $[a,b]$ with nonvanishing derivative at $a,b$. Consider the
Schr\"odinger equation $u''=\frac{2m(V-E)}{\hbar^2}u$ for a small
nondimensional parameter $h>0$ (the physical case is the scaled family; the
theorem concerns this small-$h$ family, not a variation of natural constants).
Put $B:=\int_a^b\sqrt{2m(V-E)}\,dx$ and $S:=B/h$. Then there are an
$\varepsilon(h)\le Ch$ and a constant $C_0$ such that the transmission
coefficient is
$$T(h)=e^{-2S}\bigl[1+O\bigl(\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S}\bigr)\bigr],$$
quantitatively
$$|T(h)e^{2S}-1|\le\frac{C_0[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S}]}{1-C_0[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S}]}$$
whenever the denominator is positive. The bound holds for fixed $V,E$ with the
stated separated simple turning points; rectangular walls, coalescing turning
points, barrier-top uniformity and resonant multiwell interference are excluded.

Let $q\in C^5([-x_-,x_+])$ be real, with a single simple zero at $0$:
$q(0)=0$, $q'(0)>0$, $q(x)$ has the sign of $x$, and $q\ne0$ on
$[-x_-,0)\cup(0,x_+]$. Let $h>0$ and consider $u''=q(x)u/h^2$ on the interval.
Define
$$\zeta(x):=\operatorname{sign}(x)\Bigl[\frac32\Bigl|\int_0^x\sqrt{|q(s)|}\,ds\Bigr|\Bigr]^{2/3},\qquad a(x):=(\zeta'(x))^{-1/2},\qquad u(x)=a(x)w(\zeta(x)).$$
Then:

(a) $\zeta\in C^4$, $\zeta(\zeta')^2=q$, $\zeta'>0$ with
$\min\zeta'>0$, and $a>0$ is $C^3$;

(b) $w$ satisfies $w''(\zeta)=\bigl[\zeta/h^2+R(\zeta)\bigr]w(\zeta)$ with
$$R(\zeta)=-\frac{a''(\zeta)}{a(\zeta)\,(\zeta')^2},$$
a continuous bounded real function on $\zeta([-x_-,x_+])$;

(c) the constants implicit in (a)–(b) depend only on $q$ and the interval.

Adopt the hypotheses and notation of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-liouville-turning-point-transformation]]: $q\in C^5$
with a single simple zero at $0$, $q'(0)>0$, transformed equation
$w''=[\zeta/h^2+R(\zeta)]w$ on $\zeta([-x_-,x_+])$, $a>0$ the Liouville factor
and $R$ continuous bounded. Let
$A_h(\zeta):=A(\zeta/h^{2/3})$, $B_h(\zeta):=B(\zeta/h^{2/3})$ for the Airy
functions of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-airy-envelopes-and-asymptotic-coefficients]]
(Wronskian $A_hB_h'-A_h'B_h=h^{-2/3}/\pi$), and define the envelopes
$$e_h(\zeta):=\bigl(1+|\zeta|/h^{2/3}\bigr)^{-1/4}\exp\Bigl(-\frac{2(\zeta_+)^{3/2}}{3h}\Bigr),\qquad d_h(\zeta):=h^{-2/3}\bigl(1+|\zeta|/h^{2/3}\bigr)^{1/4}\exp\Bigl(-\frac{2(\zeta_+)^{3/2}}{3h}\Bigr).$$
Then:

(a) *Volterra representation.* For $h$ small the unique solution with Airy terminal data $w(c)=A_h(c)$, $w'(c)=A_h'(c)$ at the right endpoint $\zeta=c$ satisfies
$$w(\zeta)=A_h(\zeta)+\pi h^{2/3}\int_\zeta^c\bigl[A_h(\zeta)B_h(v)-B_h(\zeta)A_h(v)\bigr]R(v)w(v)\,dv .$$

(b) *Stable weighted estimate.* There is a constant $C_A$ with
$|w(\zeta)-A_h(\zeta)|\le C_Ae_h(\zeta)(e^{\varepsilon_h}-1)$ and
$|w'(\zeta)-A_h'(\zeta)|\le C_Ad_h(\zeta)(e^{\varepsilon_h}-1)$, where
$$\varepsilon_h:=Ch\int_{-b}^c\frac{|R(v)|}{\sqrt{|v|+h^{2/3}}}\,dv\le C'h$$
for constants depending only on $q$ and the interval.

(c) *Growing branch and connection.* The solution with terminal data
$(B_h,B_h')$ at $\zeta=0$ obeys the analogous bound with $e_h$ replaced by its
growing analogue on the full interval; consequently, for fixed $\zeta>0$ and
$\zeta<0$ away from zero, the forbidden-side solution
$q^{-1/4}\exp(-\frac1h\int_0^x\sqrt q)$ corresponds to
$2(-q)^{-1/4}\sin(\frac1h\int_x^0\sqrt{-q}+\pi/4)$ on the allowed side, and the
growing forbidden solution to the corresponding cosine, with absolute errors bounded by the envelopes times $C(\varepsilon_h+h/|\zeta|^{3/2})$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $A$ be the
entire Airy function of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-airy-contour-and-fresnel-normalization]] and
define, for real $z$,
$$B(z):=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty\Bigl[\exp\bigl(-t^3/3+zt\bigr)+\sin\bigl(t^3/3+zt\bigr)\Bigr]dt .$$
Then:

(a) $B$ is well defined and smooth on $\mathbb R$, extends to an entire
solution of $B''=zB$, and the Wronskian identity
$$A(z)B'(z)-A'(z)B(z)=\frac1\pi$$
holds for all complex $z$;

(b) as $Z\to+\infty$, with $\Theta=2Z^{3/2}/3+\pi/4$,
$$B(Z)=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}Z^{-1/4}e^{2Z^{3/2}/3}\bigl(1+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr),\quad B'(Z)=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}Z^{1/4}e^{2Z^{3/2}/3}\bigl(1+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr),$$
$$B(-Z)=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}Z^{-1/4}\bigl(\cos\Theta+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr),\quad B'(-Z)=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}Z^{1/4}\bigl(\sin\Theta+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr);$$

(c) *Envelopes.* With $p(z):=1+|z|$ and $S(z):=\frac23(z_+)^{3/2}$ there is a
constant $C<\infty$ with
$$|A(z)|\le Cp(z)^{-1/4}e^{-S(z)},\quad|B(z)|\le Cp(z)^{-1/4}e^{S(z)},\quad |A'(z)|\le Cp(z)^{1/4}e^{-S(z)},\quad|B'(z)|\le Cp(z)^{1/4}e^{S(z)}$$
for all real $z$, and there is $c>0$ with
$A(z)\ge cp(z)^{-1/4}e^{-S(z)}$ for $z\ge0$.

Adopt the hypotheses and notation of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-allowed-region-wkb-coefficient-equation]]: $p\in
C^2([a,b])$ positive, $h>0$, $\theta(x)=\int_a^xp$, $w_\pm=p^{-1/2}e^{\pm
i\theta/h}$, $q=\frac{3p'^2}{4p^2}-\frac{p''}{2p}$, $M$ the fundamental matrix
of $(w_+,w_-)$ and $c=M^{-1}(y,y')^{\mathsf T}$ the coefficient curve of an exact
solution $y\in C^2([a,b])$ of $y''+\frac{p^2}{h^2}y=0$. Then for every
$x\in[a,b]$:

(a) *Growth bound.* $\|c(x)\|_1\le\|c(a)\|_1\exp\Bigl(h\displaystyle\int_a^x
\frac{|q(s)|}{p(s)}\,ds\Bigr)$.

(b) *Deviation bound.*
$$\|c(x)-c(a)\|_1\le\|c(a)\|_1\Bigl(\exp\Bigl(h\int_a^x\frac{|q(s)|}{p(s)}\,ds\Bigr)-1\Bigr).$$

(c) *Pointwise wavefunction error.* With $\Psi(x):=c_+(a)w_+(x)+c_-(a)w_-(x)$
the leading WKB wave,
$$|y(x)-\Psi(x)|\le p(x)^{-1/2}\|c(a)\|_1\Bigl(\exp\Bigl(h\int_a^x\frac{|q(s)|}{p(s)}\,ds\Bigr)-1\Bigr).$$

The estimate degenerates as $p\to0$ (turning points are excluded by the
hypotheses) and asserts nothing about connecting asymptotics across a turning
point; it is an explicit finite-interval error bound of Gronwall type.

**(a) Framework data and line model.** Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P5 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), the state and observable readings cited there, and the declared effective one-dimensional line model [[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] with a mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s=0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and units from [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] ([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a real potential $$V\in C_c^{5}(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$$ (five times continuously differentiable with compact support); it is real, bounded and measurable, so the line model's assigned energy operator $H_{V}$ of its clause (c) is defined with domain $D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$, acts by $H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}D^{2}f+Vf$, and its stationary equation at energy $E$ reads $$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,\psi''+V\psi=E\psi$$ for classically $C^{2}$ solutions. **(b) Reference scales and nondimensionalisation.** As an additional model assumption of the pair fix a **reference length** $\ell>0$ (metres) and a **reference energy** $E_\star>0$ (joules), and put $$W(\xi):=\frac{V(\ell\xi)}{E_\star},\qquad \lambda:=\frac{E}{E_\star},\qquad h:=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt{2mE_\star}} .$$ Then $W\in C_c^{5}(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$ is dimensionless with support scaled by $\ell$, and $h>0$ is dimensionless. By [[lem-nrqm-approximations-scaled-line-model-correspondence]] the physical stationary equation of clause (a) at energy $E$ is equivalent, under $x=\ell\xi$, $\psi(\ell\xi)=u(\xi)$, to the **dimensionless WKB equation** $$u''(\xi)=\frac{W(\xi)-\lambda}{h^{2}}\,u(\xi),\qquad \xi\in I,$$ on every interval $I$, and the physical WKB phase integral over a subinterval $[x_{a},x_{b}]=\ell[a,b]$ with $V>E$ (respectively $V<E$) equals $1/h$ times the corresponding dimensionless integral, as stated in clause (b) of that lemma. The pair calls $h$ the model's **semiclassical parameter** and calls $h\ll1$ the **semiclassical regime**; the physical content of the regime is $\hbar\ll\ell\sqrt{2mE_\star}$, and every statement of the page's theorems is an exact statement about the family indexed by $h$, with the error bounds stated at each $h$. **(c) Turning points, regions and phase.** For the data $(W,\lambda)$ put $$\tau:=\{\xi\in\mathbb R: W(\xi)=\lambda\}$$ for the set of **turning points**. A point $\xi_{0}\in\tau$ is **simple** when $W'(\xi_{0})\ne0$. An open interval $J$ is an **allowed interval** when $W(\xi)-\lambda<0$ on $J$ (the dimensionless kinetic energy $-(W-\lambda)$ is positive there), a **forbidden interval** when $W(\xi)-\lambda>0$ on $J$. On an allowed interval the model uses the local wavenumber $$p(\xi):=\sqrt{\lambda-W(\xi)}>0$$ and the WKB phase $\theta(\xi):=\int_{\xi_{\mathrm{ref}}}^{\xi}p(s)\,ds$ with a declared base point; on a forbidden interval the model uses $\kappa(\xi):=\sqrt{W(\xi)-\lambda}>0$. The **WKB exponent** of a forbidden interval $[\xi_{a},\xi_{b}]$ is $$S:=\int_{\xi_{a}}^{\xi_{b}}\sqrt{W(\xi)-\lambda}\,d\xi =\frac{h}{\hbar}\int_{x_{a}}^{x_{b}}\sqrt{2m(V(x)-E)}\,dx,$$ equivalently $S/h$ is the physical action in units of $\hbar$, by the lemma's clause (b) with $\xi_{a,b}=x_{a,b}/\ell$. The three declared regime hypotheses used by the page are: (W1) **Allowed-interval regularity**: $W\in C^{2}$ on a neighbourhood of $[a,b]$ and $\lambda-W\ge\delta>0$ on $[a,b]$ for some $\delta>0$ (no turning point in the interval; the interval is allowed); (W2) **Separated simple turning points**: $W-\lambda$ has exactly two zeros $\xi_{a}<\xi_{b}$ in $\mathbb R$, both simple, is positive on $(\xi_{a},\xi_{b})$ and negative on the complement of $[\xi_{a},\xi_{b}]$ (equivalently the physical barrier $V-E$ has exactly two simple zeros surrounding a forbidden region and is negative outside); (W3) **Single simple turning point**: on an interval $[\xi_{0}-r,\xi_{0}+s]$ the equation $W-\lambda$ has the single zero $\xi_{0}$, it is simple, and $W-\lambda<0$ on one side and $>0$ on the other. **(d) Declared barrier transmission reading.** For $\ell$, $E_\star$, $m$, $\hbar$, $V$, $E$ satisfying (W2), the model declares a **declared scattering solution** at energy $E$ to be a solution $u$ of the dimensionless equation which is oscillatory on both outer allowed sides with in-going/out-going WKB amplitudes fixed by the matching construction of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-two-turn-barrier-tunnelling-error]], and declares the **transmission coefficient** $T(h)$ to be the modulus-squared ratio of the out-going to the in-going amplitude in that normalization (equivalently, in the model's reading, the transmitted fraction of the reference probability current). This is a declared model quantity of the matching construction; no detector, wave packet, scattering experiment or measured count is asserted, and clause (d) does not by itself assert any formula for $T(h)$. **(e) Scope.** The model concerns a declared spinless massive particle in the declared one-dimensional line model with a compactly supported $C^{5}$ potential, at a fixed energy, in the nondimensionalised family of clause (b). It asserts nothing about two- or three-dimensional scattering, about singular or non-smooth potentials, about wave packets, detectors or measurements, and about any laboratory realization of the line model, the potential $V$ or the energy $E$.

Let $\psi_{0}$ be a normalized eigenvector, $P_{0}\psi_{0}=\psi_{0}$, let $$S:=\iota_{Q_{0}}\bigl(H_{0}|_{D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H}-E\bigr)^{-1}Q_{0}, \qquad Q_{0}=I-P_{0},$$ be the reduced inverse of the model clause (c)(iii). In the branch $v>0$ put $$R:=\frac{g}{8v}.$$ Then clauses (a)-(e) hold for every real $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<R$ in this positive-norm branch; clause (f) covers $v=0$ independently of $R$: (a) $H(\lambda)$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$; the model's followed label $E_{\lambda}$ of the contour $|z-E|=g/2$ exists, is the unique spectral value of $H(\lambda)$ inside that contour, is real, and its spectral projection is the orthogonal rank-one projection $P_{\lambda}=E_{H(\lambda)}(\{E_{\lambda}\})$; Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework, for systems in the declared massive-matter sector, the following statements about states and their composition. Assume throughout the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is the choice hypothesis of the mathematical suppliers cited below. **(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The assignment of a Hilbert space to a physical system is a model assumption; the linear structure used to combine descriptions mathematically is not an empirical claim. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it. **(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$. **(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). Thus the limit is again a density operator, without requiring the components to be orthogonal pure states. The weights are a classical preparation uncertainty and are not amplitudes. Distinct weighted ensembles of pure states may define the same $\rho$. **(iv) Composition.** Two independent distinguishable subsystems with state spaces $H_{A}$ and $H_{B}$ are composed by the completed Hilbert tensor product $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Product preparations $\psi_{A}\otimes\psi_{B}$ are the special case of preparations in which each subsystem has its own specified preparation; general composite preparations are linear combinations and mixtures and need not factor. A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). The existence of the completed tensor product is mathematics; the assignment of that product to a composite physical system is the physical assumption here. **(v) Restrictions that are separate assumptions.** Restrictions of the state space by superselection rules, identical-particle symmetry sectors, and the replacement of the tensor product by more general algebraic structures are not consequences of the clauses above: where such a restriction is used it is adopted separately, and the identical-species sectors are the subject of the postulate P6 of this page. **(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model within its declared sector. They are not derived from experiment, and they do not assert that a physical system is exactly described by such a Hilbert space; no numerical measurement is recorded. The compatibility of the framework with observation is a question about fully specified models and reported data, in the sense of P7.

If $v=0$, these data are constant for all real couplings, with no radius involving division by $v$. (ii) the **first-order operator** is the Hermitian operator $$V_{E}:=\bigl(P_{0}VP_{0}\bigr)\big|_{P_{0}\mathfrak H}$$ on the finite-dimensional eigenspace $P_{0}\mathfrak H$, whose spectrum $\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})\subseteq[-v,v]$ is the model's first-order shift data (joules per unit coupling); (iii) the **complementary reduced inverse** $$S:=\iota_{Q_{0}}\bigl(H_{0}|_{D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H}-E\bigr)^{-1}Q_{0}$$ is a bounded operator with the displayed exact complementary-domain inverse. For $r=1$ it is supplied by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-simple-level-reduced-resolvent-coefficients]]; for general finite $r$ it is $\iota_{Q_0}B_0(E)Q_0$, where $B_0(E)$ is the inverse in clause (a) of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-degenerate-feshbach-error]] at zero coupling and $z=E$. Its role is to record that the **whole** complementary spectral subspace, continuum included, contributes to the second-order data. **(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) cover bounded perturbations of a self-adjoint operator and a fixed isolated finite-multiplicity label only. The definition asserts no time-dependent perturbation, no adiabatic ramping of $\lambda$, no statement that a preparation occupies the branch of $E_{\lambda}$ or of any eigenvalue of $V_{E}$, no branch-population or relaxation statement, no measurement and no identification of the model with a laboratory system; the labels $E_{\lambda}$ are spectral data of the declared family.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, $l\ge0$, $k>0$, let $A_l$ be the radial operator of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]], write $$j:=\frac{\gamma}{2k}-l-1,$$ and for $a=2l+1$ and $n\in\mathbb N_0$ let $$L_n^{(a)}(x):=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^i\binom{n+a}{n-i}\frac{x^i}{i!}$$ be the $n$-th Laguerre polynomial of order $a$. Then: (a) *substitution.* A $C^2$ function $u$ on $(0,\infty)$ satisfies $-u''+(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r)u=-k^2u$ if and only if $v(x):=e^{x/2}x^{-(l+1)}u(x/2k)$ is $C^2$ and satisfies $xv''+(2l+2-x)v'+jv=0$ on $(0,\infty)$; (b) *regular series.* With $v_0:=1$ and $$v_{i+1}:=\frac{(i-j)v_i}{(i+1)(i+2l+2)}\qquad(i\ge0),$$ the power series $v(x):=\sum_{i\ge0}v_ix^i$ converges for every $x\in\mathbb R$ and defines a solution of $xv''+(2l+2-x)v'+jv=0$ on $\mathbb R$; (c) *regular solution and general solution.* The function $$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r):=r^{l+1}e^{-kr}v(2kr)$$ is a $C^\infty$ solution of the radial equation on $(0,\infty)$ with $u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)/r^{l+1}\to1$ as $r\downarrow0$; it is, up to a nonzero scalar multiple, the only solution with $u(r)/r^{l+1}$ bounded as $r\downarrow0$; every solution of the radial equation on $(0,\infty)$ is $c_1u_{\mathrm{reg}}+c_2u_2$ with $u_2$ defined near zero by $u_2(r):=u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)\int_{r_*}^r u_{\mathrm{reg}}(s)^{-2}ds$, where $0<r_*<\delta$ and $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$ has no zero in $(0,\delta)$, and extended uniquely to $(0,\infty)$ by the regular initial-value equation, and every solution that is not a multiple of $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$ has $|u(r)|/r$ unbounded as $r\downarrow0$; (d) *termination.* $v$ is a polynomial if and only if $j\in\mathbb N_0$; in that case $v$ is a nonzero constant multiple of $L_j^{(2l+1)}$, and $$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)=c\,r^{l+1}e^{-kr}L_j^{(2l+1)}(2kr)\quad(c\ne0)$$ lies in $L^2(0,\infty;dr)$; (e) *eigenfunction.* If $j\in\mathbb N_0$ then $u_{\mathrm{reg}}\in D(A_l)$ and $A_lu_{\mathrm{reg}}=-k^2u_{\mathrm{reg}}$; equivalently, for every $m$ the transported function $\psi(r\Omega):=u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ lies in $H^2(\mathbb R^3)\cap D(C)$ and satisfies $C\psi=-k^2\psi$. The assertions are statements about the ordinary differential equation and the operators $A_l,C$; no physical interpretation of $\gamma,k$ or of any spectral level is made.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice hypothesis used by the change-of-variables lemma cited below. For every real $\lambda>0$ and every integer $k\ge0$ the function $r\mapsto r^{k}e^{-\lambda r}$ is Lebesgue integrable on $(0,\infty)$ and $$\int_0^\infty r^{k}e^{-\lambda r}\,dr=\frac{k!}{\lambda^{k+1}}.$$ The assertion is an identity for the Lebesgue integral of a nonnegative Borel function; no probabilistic interpretation and no normalised density are asserted. In particular no statement is made about any other exponent, about complex $\lambda$, or about negative powers.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $P_l$ be the Legendre polynomials of [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-legendre-rodrigues-equation]], and for $l\in\mathbb N$ and $0\le m\le l$ define the function $w_{lm}:(-1,1)\to\mathbb R$ by $$w_{lm}(t):=(-1)^m(1-t^2)^{m/2}\,\frac{d^m}{dt^m}P_l(t),$$ where $(1-t^2)^{1/2}>0$ denotes the nonnegative square root. Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on $S^2$ and let the angle coordinates be $\Phi(\theta,\varphi)=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta)$ ([[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]). Then: (a) each $w_{lm}$ extends continuously to $[-1,1]$, with $w_{lm}(\pm1)=0$ when $m\ge1$, and on $(-1,1)$ it satisfies the associated Legendre equation $$-\bigl((1-t^2)w_{lm}'\bigr)'+\frac{m^2}{1-t^2}w_{lm}=l(l+1)w_{lm}\qquad(-1<t<1),$$ equivalently $(1-t^2)w_{lm}''-2tw_{lm}'+\Bigl[l(l+1)-\frac{m^2}{1-t^2}\Bigr]w_{lm}=0$; (b) for fixed $m\ge0$ the functions $w_{lm}$, $l\ge m$, are pairwise orthogonal in $L^2((-1,1),dt)$: $\int_{-1}^1w_{lm}w_{km}\,dt=0$ for $k\ne l$; moreover $0<\int_{-1}^1w_{lm}^2\,dt<+\infty$; (c) with $b_{lm}:=\bigl(\int_{-1}^1w_{lm}^2\,dt\bigr)^{-1/2}>0$ and $$Y_{lm}(\theta,\varphi):=b_{lm}\,w_{lm}(\cos\theta)\,\frac{e^{im\varphi}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\qquad(l\ge m\ge0),$$ extended by $Y_{l,-m}:=(-1)^m\overline{Y_{lm}}$ for $m\ge1$ (as functions of $(\theta,\varphi)\in(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)$, $\overline{\ \cdot\ }$ denoting complex conjugation, [[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]), one has $|Y_{l,-m}|=|Y_{lm}|$ and $\overline{Y_{lm}}=(-1)^mY_{l,-m}$ for all $l$ and all $m$ with $|m|\le l$; (d) the family $\{Y_{lm}:l\ge0,\ -l\le m\le l\}$ is orthonormal in $L^2(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]): for all $(l,m)\ne(l',m')$ with $|m|\le l$, $|m'|\le l'$, the integral $\int_{S^2}Y_{lm}\overline{Y_{l'm'}}\,d\sigma$ equals $0$, and it equals $1$ when $(l,m)=(l',m')$; (e) $w_{l0}=P_l$, and $w_{ll}(t)=(-1)^l\frac{(2l)!}{2^l l!}(1-t^2)^{l/2}$. The functions $Y_{lm}$ are complex-valued $L^2$-functions on the sphere; no physical interpretation as angular momentum eigenfunctions or spherical harmonics of an atom is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on $S^2$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]) and let $(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,\ -l\le m\le l}$ be the functions of [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]] ([[def-complex-exponential]]). Then $(Y_{lm})$ is a complete orthonormal family of the complex Hilbert space $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]): the family is orthonormal, and if $F\in L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ satisfies $\int_{S^2}F\overline{Y_{lm}}\,d\sigma=0$ for all $l\ge0$ and $-l\le m\le l$, then $F=0$ almost everywhere. Consequently every $F$ has the expansion $$F=\sum_{l=0}^\infty\sum_{m=-l}^{l}\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle Y_{lm},\qquad \|F\|^2=\sum_{l,m}|\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle|^2,$$ with $\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle=\int_{S^2}F\overline{Y_{lm}}\,d\sigma$ and finite-subset-net convergence ([[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $S^2:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ and let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on $S^2$ of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], a finite Borel measure ([[def-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). Let $$\Phi:(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)\to S^2,\qquad \Phi(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta),$$ and let $H:=\{(x,y,0)\in\mathbb R^3:x\ge0\}$ denote the closed half-plane, a Lebesgue-null Borel set ([[thm-affine-hyperplanes-and-proper-subspaces-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]). Then: (a) for every Borel function $F:S^2\to[0,+\infty]$, $$\int_{S^2}F\,d\sigma=\int_{(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)}F\bigl(\Phi(\theta,\varphi)\bigr)\,\sin\theta\ d(\theta,\varphi),$$ the right-hand integral being the Lebesgue integral over the open rectangle; (b) $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$; (c) the identity of (a) holds with $F\in L^1(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$ in the sense that $F\circ\Phi$ is Lebesgue integrable on the rectangle against $\sin\theta\,d(\theta,\varphi)$ and the two integrals agree (real and imaginary parts, positive and negative parts).

derivations.claim: [The compressed matrices and their nonzero entry] Write $a=a_{\mu}$. From [L5], $\|u_{10}\|_{2}^{2}=4a^{-3}2!/(2/a)^{3}=1$ and $\|u_{21}\|_{2}^{2}=(24a^{5})^{-1}4!/(1/a)^{5}=1$; the explicit Kummer solutions therefore give the normalized bound states with the stated labels. For their positive real representatives, $\int_{S^{2}}Y_{10}\Omega_{3}Y_{00}\,d\sigma=(\sqrt3/(4\pi))2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}t^{2}dt=1/\sqrt3$. Their radial dipole integral is $\int_{0}^{\infty}r u_{21}u_{10}\,dr=(1/\sqrt6)a^{-4}4!/(3/(2a))^{5}=256a/(81\sqrt6)>0$. The absolutely convergent factorization [L2] yields $\langle\psi_{210},Q_{3}\psi_{100}\rangle=128\sqrt2 a/243>0$. Since $D_{3}=-qQ_{3}$, its matrix element is $-128\sqrt2 q a/243$ before rephasing. Set $\psi_{1}=\psi_{100}$ and $\psi_{2}=-\psi_{210}$ to obtain the positive off-diagonal value $D_{\rm rel}=128\sqrt2 q a/243$ without changing energies, labels or normalization. By [L2], bound states lie in all coordinate domains; all diagonal entries vanish by degree selection, and the off-diagonal $Q_{\pm}$ entries vanish by weight selection. Thus $D^{W}_{1}=D^{W}_{2}=0$ and $D^{W}_{3}=D_{\rm rel}\sigma_{1}$ with $D_{\rm rel}>0$, proving (a). [L1, L2, L5, given, algebra]

[The two-state family] In the orthonormal basis $(\psi_{1},\psi_{2})$ one has $\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}|_{W}=\operatorname{diag}(E_{1},E_{2})$ by [L1] and orthogonality of distinct eigenstates; with $v:=D_{\rm rel}(1\ \mathrm{V\, m^{-1}})$ in joules one has $V=-v\sigma_{1}$ and $$H_{S}=\begin{pmatrix}E_{1}&-v\lambda\\-v\lambda&E_{2}\end{pmatrix}.$$ Since $\sigma_{1}$ is Hermitian with $\|\sigma_{1}\|=1$, $V$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm $v$; the exact eigenvalues of a matrix $\begin{pmatrix}a&w\\w&b\end{pmatrix}$ with real $w$ are $\frac{a+b}{2}\pm\sqrt{(\frac{a-b}{2})^{2}+w^{2}}$, verified by the same direct eigenvector computation as in the two-level example of this page with $g:=\Delta$, $w:=-v\lambda$; substituting $a=E_{1},b=E_{2}$ gives clause (b). [L1, given, algebra]

[Coefficients] The label $E=E_{1}$ is simple with gap $\Delta$ (the second level is $E_{2}=E_{1}+\Delta$ and there are no further levels in the two-dimensional model); the perturbation $V$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm $v$; hence [L3] applies for $|\lambda|v<\Delta/8$. Since $V$ has vanishing diagonal, $E'(0)=\langle V\psi_{1},\psi_{1}\rangle=0$. The reduced inverse on $Q_{0}W=\mathbb C\psi_{2}$ is $S=\Delta^{-1}|\psi_{2}\rangle\langle\psi_{2}|$, so $SV\psi_{1}=-(v/\Delta)\psi_{2}$ and $VSV\psi_{1}=(v^{2}/\Delta)\psi_{1}$, giving $E''(0)=-2v^{2}/\Delta$; substituting $v=D_{\rm rel}(1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}})$ and expanding the closed form of clause (b) by [L4] gives the displayed quadratic Stark shift. This is clause (c). [L3, L4, step 1.2, algebra]

[The finite remainder check at the true half radius] At $\mathcal E=\Delta/(16D_{\rm rel})$, $\lambda v=D_{\rm rel}\mathcal E=\Delta/16$ and hence $\lambda=R/2$ for $R=\Delta/(8v)$. The page's bound is $Rv(1/2)^{3}/(1-1/2)=Rv/4=\Delta/32$. The exact lower branch satisfies $F_{-}=E_{1}+\Delta/2-\sqrt{\Delta^{2}/4+\Delta^{2}/256}=E_{1}+\Delta(8-\sqrt{65})/16$, whereas its quadratic truncation is $E_{1}-(\lambda v)^{2}/\Delta=E_{1}-\Delta/256$. Therefore $|F_{-}-E_{1}+\Delta/256|=\Delta(129-16\sqrt{65})/256=\Delta/[256(129+16\sqrt{65})]$ by [L4]. Since $129+16\sqrt{65}>128$, this remainder is strictly less than $\Delta/32768$, and consequently less than $\Delta/32$. This proves (d) without a decimal approximation. [L3, L4, step 2.1, algebra]

[Scope] The argument used the declared two-state truncation, the adopted coupling, the model's exact spectrum and the page's theorem; no laboratory atom, measured shift, polarizability, transition rate or uncompressed linear potential entered. citations.quote: Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and $r=2s+1$, together with the angular momentum readings of [[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]], [[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]), and assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ be the outcome law of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$, and for a unit vector $n=(n_{1},n_{2},n_{3})\in\mathbb R^{3}$ put $S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$, the matrix action of the self-adjoint matrix $\hbar\,n\cdot J$ on the internal factor. Then: (a) for every unit $n$ the operator $S_{n}$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator on $H_{s}$ with spectrum $\sigma(S_{n})=\hbar\{-s,-s+1,\dots,s\}$, and for each $m\in\{-s,\dots,s\}$ the eigenspace $\ker(S_{n}-\hbar m)$ is the range of the fibrewise orthogonal projection $P_{n,m}$ onto the eigenline of the matrix $n\cdot J$ with eigenvalue $m$; consequently, for every unit $\psi\in H_{s}$, $$\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar m\})=\|P_{n,m}\psi\|^{2}=\langle P_{n,m}\psi,\psi\rangle\qquad(m=-s,\dots,s),$$ and the law is concentrated on the finite set $\hbar\{-s,\dots,s\}$; (b) the Casimir operator $S^{2}=S_{x}^{2}+S_{y}^{2}+S_{z}^{2}$ equals $\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$ as a bounded operator, so for every preparation $\rho$ the law of $S^{2}$ is the Dirac law at $\hbar^{2}s(s+1)$, and one has the commutation relations $[S_{i},S_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}S_{k}$ and $[S^{2},S_{i}]=0$ on $H_{s}$, componentwise on the internal factor; (c) for $s=\tfrac12$, every unit $n$ and every unit $\psi\in H_{1/2}$ one has $$P_{n,\pm}=\tfrac12\bigl(I\pm n\cdot\sigma\bigr),\qquad \mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}\Bigl(\Bigl\{\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr) =\frac{1}{2}\Bigl(1\pm\langle(n\cdot\sigma)\psi,\psi\rangle\Bigr),$$ where $n\cdot\sigma$ is applied fibrewise; in particular, $\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar/2\})+\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{-\hbar/2\})=1$ and each number lies in $[0,1]$; (d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5 and P6 and the cited finite-dimensional mathematics; they concern the internal factor of the model. They assert no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no measurement or apparatus model, no joint measurement of two spin components, no value of $\hbar$ and no empirical spin value. In particular the statements do not identify the operators $S_{n}$ with any laboratory spin measurement, and they contain no comparison with data.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$, together with the effective magnetic-moment coupling adopted in [[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] and the angular momentum readings of [[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]], and assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix a real constant $B_{z}\in\mathbb R$ and use the uniform static field profile $\mathbf B(x):=(0,0,B_{z})$, so that the Zeeman energy operator of the postulate is $$H_{Z}=H_{0}-\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3},\qquad H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad D(H_{Z})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$ with flow $U_{Z}(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}$, and put $\omega:=\gamma_{s}B_{z}$ with unit $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. For a unit vector $\psi\in H_{s}$ put $\psi(t):=U_{Z}(t)\psi$ and $\langle S_{i}\rangle(t):=\langle S_{i}\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$. Then: (a) $H_{Z}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{Z})$ and $$U_{Z}(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\,e^{it\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$ so in particular the transverse means satisfy, for every $t$, $$\langle S_{1}\rangle(t)=\cos(\omega t)\langle S_{1}\rangle(0)+\sin(\omega t)\langle S_{2}\rangle(0),\qquad \langle S_{2}\rangle(t)=\cos(\omega t)\langle S_{2}\rangle(0)-\sin(\omega t)\langle S_{1}\rangle(0),$$ and the transverse vector $\bigl(\langle S_{1}\rangle(t),\langle S_{2}\rangle(t)\bigr)$ is the rotation of $\bigl(\langle S_{1}\rangle(0),\langle S_{2}\rangle(0)\bigr)$ by the angle $-\omega t$ in the $(1,2)$-plane; (b) the component along the field is conserved: $S_{3}U_{Z}(t)=U_{Z}(t)S_{3}$ and $\langle S_{3}\rangle(t)=\langle S_{3}\rangle(0)$ for every unit $\psi$ and every $t$; more generally the outcome law of $S_{3}$ is time-independent in every preparation; (c) the conjugation identities $$e^{itH_{Z}/\hbar}S_{1}e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}=\cos(\omega t)S_{1}+\sin(\omega t)S_{2},\qquad e^{itH_{Z}/\hbar}S_{2}e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}=\cos(\omega t)S_{2}-\sin(\omega t)S_{1}$$ hold as bounded operator identities, and with $S^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$ (the Casimir operator of the model) also $S^{2}U_{Z}(t)=U_{Z}(t)S^{2}$; (d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and the adopted coupling; it concerns the uniform static field $\mathbf B=(0,0,B_{z})$ with $B_{z}\in\mathbb R$ and the declared isolated model. It excludes inhomogeneous and time-dependent fields, spin-dependent spatial potentials, radiation, relaxation and environment coupling, asserts no measured precession frequency and no measured gyromagnetic parameter, and identifies no apparatus: $\omega=\gamma_{s}B_{z}$ is a model quantity computed from assigned model parameters.

Adopt the framework data and the declared perturbed-family model of [[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-perturbed-family-model]] with $H_{0}$ self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$, $V=V^{*}\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$, $v=\|V\|>0$, $H(\lambda)=H_{0}+\lambda V$ on $D(H_{0})$ for real $\lambda$, and an isolated eigenvalue $E$ of $H_{0}$ of **finite multiplicity $r\ge1$** with gap at least $g>0$, $\operatorname{dist}(E,\sigma(H_{0})\setminus\{E\})\ge g$. Let $P_{0}=E_{H_{0}}(\{E\})$, $Q_{0}=I-P_{0}$, and $$V_{E}:=\bigl(P_{0}VP_{0}\bigr)\big|_{P_{0}\mathfrak H}$$ the first-order operator of the model clause (c)(ii). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the suppliers. Then for every real $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|v<g/4$: (a) $H(\lambda)$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$; (b) for every real $z$ with $|z-E|+|\lambda|v\le g/2$, the restricted operator $T_{\lambda}(z):=Q_{0}(H(\lambda)-z)Q_{0}$ on $Q_{0}D(H_{0})=D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H$ has a bounded two-sided inverse $B(z):Q_{0}\mathfrak H\to Q_{0}D(H_{0})$ with $\|B(z)\|\le4/g$; (c) every real eigenvalue $z$ of $H(\lambda)$ with eigenvector $\psi\ne0$ and $|z-E|+|\lambda|v\le g/2$ lies within the first-order shift set: $$\operatorname{dist}\bigl(z,\,E+\lambda\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})\bigr) \le\frac{4\lambda^{2}v^{2}}{g},$$ where $\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})\subseteq[-v,v]$ is the spectrum of the Hermitian operator $V_{E}$ on the $r$-dimensional eigenspace; moreover $P_{0}\psi\ne0$ for every such eigenvector. Every eigenvalue in the model's followed cluster inside $|z-E|<g/2$ lies in this controlled window and therefore obeys the same bound; (d) *first-order content.* The eigenvalues of $V_{E}$ are the model's first-order shifts: the set $E+\lambda\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})$ has at most $r$ points, all within $|\lambda|v$ of $E$; the entire followed cluster, and every other eigenvalue in the window of (c), are localised at distance $O(\lambda^{2}v^{2}/g)$ from this set, and no ordering or one-to-one correspondence between the $r$ spectral branches and the points of $\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})$ is asserted; (e) *No relaxation or selection.* The theorem is a statement about the spectra of the declared family. It asserts no instantaneous transition of any preparation to the branch of the smallest value of $\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})$, no relaxation to a lowest branch, no equilibration and no measurement; which spectral subspace a preparation occupies is fixed by the preparation and by the evolution postulate P4 of the declared model, not by the label $E_{\lambda}$; (f) the theorem is conditional on the strict positive gap, on the finite multiplicity of $E$ and on the boundedness of $V$; it asserts nothing about degenerate essential-spectrum labels, gap-closing families, unbounded perturbations or time-dependent couplings.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt P1, P2 and P4 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, with the state, sharp-observable and evolution readings of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical suppliers. **(b) The perturbed family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair, fix a self-adjoint operator $H_{0}:D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H\to\mathfrak H$ on the declared state space, **declare** $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ to be the unperturbed sharp energy observable, fix a bounded self-adjoint operator $V\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) with $$v:=\|V\|<\infty$$ ([[def-operator-norm]]) and fix a real **coupling** $\lambda$ (dimensionless: $\lambda V$ is read in joules).
